scope: Post hoc qualitative sample from terminal reserved photo arms. Catalog identities, classifier identities, policy names, aggregate outcomes and source photo metadata withheld. Not a random accuracy sample or human ground truth. Coding-harness reviewer compute is outside the recorded experiment API ledger.
method: All 11 exact supplied JPEGs were inspected through view_image at original detail. Each A–D assignment was assessed separately against its own full supplied catalog. No cross-catalog ID equivalence, hidden identity or aggregate score was used.

fit_definitions.supported: Visible focal subject fits the catalog membership wording.
fit_definitions.plausible: Reasonable membership or rejection under an ambiguous boundary, missing category or uncertain object function; not a demonstrated error.
fit_definitions.unsupported: Visible focal subject conflicts with the assigned category; the reason and nearest reasonable alternative are stated.
fit_definitions.unclear: Insufficient visible evidence for a defensible membership judgment.

severity_definition: Severity describes a supported concern about this assignment, not a population error score; plausible boundary choices with no demonstrated error have severity none.
limits: Post hoc qualitative selected sample; no population accuracy estimate.
Automated Codex same-family review, not independent human truth.
Object purpose, source metadata and identities were not looked up or inferred from opaque filenames.
Catalog coverage differs, so an Other response can be defensible even when another catalog offers a fitting name.

cases.visible_subject: A torn aircraft-like passenger-cabin section with exposed seat rows and metal framing, outdoors.
literal_evidence: A curved, ripped outer shell encloses several parallel rows of passenger seats.
Internal ribs, hanging wiring and broken panels are exposed.
Trees and pavement surround the wrecked cabin; they are background rather than the focal subject.
uncertainty: The exact aircraft type, cause of damage, location and whether this is a staged display cannot be established from the pixels.
Catalog A uses motor vehicles with road-vehicle examples; including an aircraft under that wording is reasonable but less explicit than catalog C's transport-vehicle wording.

A.reason: The focal object is damaged transport-cabin wreckage, not a building, room interior or fixed civic structure. Exposed structural framing alone does not make it architecture.

nearest_alternative.reason: Vehicles is the nearest named category: an aircraft is motorized transport, although this catalog only gives road-vehicle examples.

B.reason: The recognizable passenger-cabin wreckage is a vehicle subject; parked/displayed/in-use examples do not require an intact vehicle.

C.reason: The main object is recognizable transport-vehicle wreckage with passenger seating, fitting the explicit transport-vehicle scope.

D.reason: The vehicle remains the primary subject despite its damaged and stationary condition; road vehicles are examples rather than an exhaustive list.

cases.visible_subject: An apparently nonliving display mannequin wearing a red jacket and trousers over a printed shirt.
literal_evidence: A glossy red jacket, red trousers and a motorcycle-print shirt occupy most of the frame.
The exposed head/neck surface is featureless and the hands appear rigid and mannequin-like.
There is no visible human action or social scene; the framing presents an outfit.
themes: living person versus crafted display figure
uncertainty: The upper head is cropped, so a live model cannot be ruled out with absolute certainty, but the visible featureless surface and rigid hands strongly favor a mannequin.
Treating a garment-display mannequin as an artistic/display object is a defensible coarse substitute in catalogs without an apparel category; it need not mean the outfit itself is an artwork.

A.reason: The visible evidence favors an inanimate mannequin used to showcase garments, rather than a portrait or scene centered on a living person. This catalog has a more direct clothing category.

nearest_alternative.reason: Clothing and Accessories explicitly covers garments shown as the main subject.

B.reason: People requires a person or their activity as the subject. An apparently nonliving clothing-display figure is a weaker fit, and clothing alone does not establish a person-centered scene.

nearest_alternative.reason: Art and Decorative Objects includes crafted display objects and treats depicted figures as objects; Other is also reasonable if a commercial mannequin is outside that scope.

C.reason: A mannequin is a crafted human figure photographed as an object, so the crafted-figure scope provides a reasonable fit despite the main emphasis on clothing.

D.reason: The figure appears nonliving and is presented as a display object, which is compatible with the crafted-display scope. The absence of an apparel category makes this an approximate boundary choice.

cases.visible_subject: An ornate circular metal relief disk set into surrounding pavement, with a central face and rings of symbols.
literal_evidence: The frame is dominated by a round metal disk with a raised central face and dense concentric decorative motifs.
A pale circular rim and surrounding paving are visible at its edges.
No person, animal, vehicle or powered equipment is the focal subject.
uncertainty: The image does not establish whether the disk is a working utility cover, an installed decorative plaque or another ornamental surface.
Close framing emphasizes the relief design, while its apparent placement in pavement also supports an infrastructure reading.

A.reason: This catalog explicitly includes manhole covers and street fixtures. The disk appears set into pavement, so infrastructure is reasonable, although a utility function is not visually proven.

nearest_alternative.reason: Art and Crafts also fits the prominently photographed decorative relief object.

B.reason: The visible focal subject is an elaborately crafted relief object. Its decorative design supports the artwork/display-object category even if the object also serves an infrastructure function.

C.reason: The frame presents the ornamented crafted object and its relief figures, fitting art and decorative objects. Buildings and infrastructure remains a plausible secondary reading if this is a utility cover.

D.reason: The ornate metal relief is a clear crafted/decorative object. The alternative architecture category could also be reasonable if its unconfirmed utility-cover function is prioritized.

cases.visible_subject: A masked player crouching behind a red inflatable barrier and aiming a paintball marker, with a striped official in the background.
literal_evidence: The foreground person wears a full protective face mask and holds a marker with a hopper.
The person crouches beside a large red inflatable obstacle marked with colored paint spots.
Another masked person wears a vertically striped shirt behind the player.
uncertainty: The exact competition, participants and venue are unknown; the visible equipment strongly supports a paintball-game interpretation.

A.reason: The image centers on a person actively participating in a physical game, matching Sports and Physical Activities rather than the catalog's nonsporting People category.

B.reason: People explicitly includes sports and equipment when the photograph centers on a person or their activity.

C.reason: The scene is centered on people and their sporting activity, explicitly within this category.

D.reason: The person and athletic game activity are the focus; the People description explicitly includes athletes.

cases.visible_subject: A wall-mounted numbered dartboard with darts and several keys or key-like metal objects attached to it.
literal_evidence: A circular board is divided into numbered radial scoring wedges with colored rings.
Several red-finned darts and metal keys or key-like objects project from the board.
The board occupies nearly the entire frame; no player is visible.
uncertainty: The unusual arrangement may be a playful decorative/art display, or simply a functional dartboard used to hold objects. Its intended purpose is not established.
A's sports category is phrased around people participating, while B/C/D lack an explicit sports-equipment category; none straightforwardly guarantees a named fit for an unoccupied dartboard.

A.reason: Other is defensible for a game target shown without a participant: the sports category explicitly describes people in sport, and the board is not clearly an artwork.

nearest_alternative.reason: Art and Crafts is possible if the unusual board-and-key arrangement is treated as a crafted decorative display.

B.reason: The colored target and unusual collection of keys can reasonably be read as a crafted display object. However, a functional dartboard is not automatically an artwork, so this is a boundary judgment.

nearest_alternative.reason: Other remains reasonable because no category clearly names games or non-electrical sporting equipment.

C.reason: No category clearly covers a functional game target without a person. Rejecting it avoids forcing the board into art or workshop hardware.

nearest_alternative.reason: Art and decorative objects is possible if the image is interpreted as a deliberately decorative arrangement.

D.reason: Other is reasonable when the primary object is game equipment and neither a person nor an unambiguous decorative artwork is shown.

nearest_alternative.reason: Art and decorative objects could cover an intentionally crafted display, but that purpose is uncertain.

cases.visible_subject: A small gold-colored cross engraved with religious words, resting on pale woven fabric.
literal_evidence: A shaped metallic cross lies diagonally across textured light fabric.
Engraved lettering is visible along the cross arms and vertical stem.
The object itself fills the foreground; no living person is shown.
uncertainty: The image does not establish whether the cross is jewelry, a handheld devotional item or a standalone ornament; no chain or attachment is clearly visible.

A.reason: The shaped and engraved cross is a crafted decorative/symbolic object, directly compatible with Art and Crafts.

B.reason: A deliberately crafted and inscribed cross photographed as an object fits the artwork/decorative-display scope.

C.reason: The main subject is a crafted decorative object rather than a living figure, matching this category.

D.reason: The close-up centers on an engraved crafted object, fitting Art and decorative objects.

cases.visible_subject: A metal cooking range with several circular burners, front control knobs and an open lower oven or cabinet, with cleaning gloves draped over its edge.
literal_evidence: Several ring-shaped burners are mounted on the top of a metal cooking unit.
A row of knobs runs across its front, and its lower compartment stands open.
Yellow cleaning gloves and a sponge rest on the top edge; pipes or a hose are visible at the side.
uncertainty: The burner and pipe arrangement suggests a gas cooking appliance, but the image cannot establish whether it also has electrical components or ignition.

Electrical/electronic categories do not unambiguously cover a nonelectrical gas range. Broad non-electrical work-equipment wording in B is another possible interpretation, while the other hardware categories emphasize manual/workshop implements.

A.reason: The appliance dominates the frame; this is not chiefly a room interior, building or fixed public infrastructure. A piece of equipment inside a building does not make the focal subject architectural.

nearest_alternative.reason: Other avoids forcing a cooking range into electrical components or architecture when there is no clear general-appliance category.

B.reason: Other is defensible because a gas cooking range is not clearly electrical/electronic and no category explicitly names appliances.

nearest_alternative.reason: Tools and Work Equipment broadly includes non-electrical work equipment, which could cover a commercial cooking range, although the examples emphasize workshop tools.

C.reason: Other is a reasonable response to a cooking appliance that is not clearly electrical, manual workshop tooling, food, or the surrounding built environment.

nearest_alternative.reason: Electrical and electronic equipment would be possible if this range has relevant electrical operation, but that is not established by the photograph.

D.reason: The catalog lacks a general cooking-appliance category, and the object is not clearly electrical. Rejecting this boundary case is more defensible than classifying its background interior.

nearest_alternative.reason: Electrical and electronic equipment is an alternative only if the cooking unit is interpreted as electrical equipment, which is uncertain from the pixels.
